title: I1-phase-xsession-directive.md.txt
body:
# Phase directive — «Cross-session prefix ledger row» (Epoch 4, viola-0.2.0; the head entry at `3d281c17`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped. A fact the
plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

The operator is AWAY from THIS session (he answers through the overseer's dialogs, and he is at hand today): raise
NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the
options in order with each one's cost, the recommendation marked) and the step stops there, saying so. A technical
fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start and reads nothing of the
operator's real `~/.claude*`.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-21 — cite them as this directive's

- A bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.330 (mise `latest`), and THIS session runs it; the pinned product reads it
  `verified` from a 24-row stamp in the live home (stamps of 2.1.328 and 2.1.330 stand there). The pinned product
  (the release build of `a59da9da`) holds none of the last five mends and is untouched until its re-pin.
- The tree at `3d281c17` holds 28 relied ledger rows and ONE stamped fixture set (2.1.328); both default-version
  constants read 2.1.328; the identity floor is thirteen names; the automatic verify stands behind
  `verify_new_cli`, default off.
- The entry's carry holds what the last chunk measured and what the operator already answered: start `HF`
  (2.1.328 by path, the rig's scratch home and private config) read the cross-session row `fail` (`no-prompt`) —
  the sender exited 0, no UserPromptSubmit reached Run B within 30 s, no dialog stood in Run B after it. Three
  causes were not told apart (hypothesis, each unmeasured): the model did not call the send tool · the deferred
  send tool could not be reached · the session-id target was not resolved. His earlier answers stand for this
  entry: path (A), a print-mode CLI sender whose one allowed tool is the CLI's own cross-session send; the
  compiled `accept` settings literal on Run B. Everything cut from the last chunk was cut whole: this plan writes
  it again.
- The documentation leaves hold no figure the code states: this chunk adds none.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `3d281c17`, nothing wider: the `cross-session-prefix`
   relied row (v2-25), its sender, Run B's settings literal, stamped live. The carried rehearsal red is acted on
   only at its next red. Every carry is disposed by name in the plan.
2. **The cause of `no-prompt` is settled FIRST, with NO start.** At P3, from what can be read without one — the
   installed 2.1.328 and 2.1.330 bundles, the last chunk's evidence in the store, the cut code in git history —
   say for each of the three causes what the bundle states and what stays unmeasured:
   - how a DEFERRED tool is reached under a print-mode start with a one-tool allow-list (whether the allow-list
     must also name the tool-search tool, whether a deferred tool is callable by name at all in that mode, what
     the sender's prompt must say);
   - the ADDRESS form the send tool's lookup takes (a session id, a name, a prefix), what it resolves against
     and under WHICH config dir — whether a sender under the rig's private config can see Run B at all;
   - whether delivery into Run B needs Run B idle, a registry entry written, a peer setting beyond the `accept`
     literal, or a minimum uptime;
   - whether any of this moved between 2.1.328 and 2.1.330, and WHICH version the row is stamped on.
3. **A diagnostic reading is a widening the operator has NOT seen.** If the plan wants the sender's tool calls by
   NAME, or the send tool's result class, kept as closed words: say exactly what is read, from where (the sender's
   stdout stream, a transcript, a hook payload), what is kept, where it is written, and the proof that no prompt
   text, tool input or model text reaches any file, stamp, fixture or log. It is a fork of its own in the block.
4. **Every master row whose words the change reaches: search ALL seven masters before the block is written**
   (verify's child set and its runs, the residual rows, the settings Run B carries, what leaves the process, the
   ledger's rows, the harness prefix, the automatic verify — the sender now also runs there, with no human, in a
   user's real config) and name EVERY reached row, with the ones read as not reached beside them. Rows the last
   chunk's wrap left unamended because their ground was cut are named again here. A widening is said as one HERE,
   whole; a row found reached AFTER the block is a fork of its own.
5. **At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`:** your window; the cause as the bundle
   reads it and what only a start can tell; the answer path recommended and the ones set aside, each with how it
   fails; every reached master row; every live start's SHAPE before the count — processes, every byte typed,
   every dialog raised and how it is answered, the stop, every file written and where, under WHICH home; for each
   start a predicate its reading can FAIL, the red reading named; what each start READS (key names, counts, closed
   words — never a text) and from WHERE; whether any typed key or answered dialog moves the wheel before a send;
   which versions are stamped and what a 29th relied row does to every stamped version and the one fixture set;
   the capability's concretized claim and what «verified» would rest on; a recommended cap and what one spare
   would be for; whether one implement window holds it. The cap, any key or byte into a CLI dialog, any widening,
   what «verified» rests on and any read or write under his real home are the operator's: the block WAITS.
6. **For every capped start, name what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree** (a kept stamp, a kept
   dir, a scratch, a runtime dir — the last chunk's kept `HF`/`HG` products among them), each with a no-start
   gate entry right before the start, placed so a round resumed at one entry still fires it; a start whose
   product is kept gets an entry that reads it AFTER.
7. One ledger, one count: `--cap` is the RUNNING total of base starts in the ledger file. A census entry after
   the LAST live leg is keyed to the operator leg.
8. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases AND building the whole workspace where the
   case needs a root binary; the bound that applies is the entry's own timeout key, ids within 16 characters.
   Every filter term of a gate entry SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag. An expect atom must be able
   to fail; a word that may honestly read two ways is a READING recorded, not a failing atom. The row keeps its
   red: one case where Run B, started with the literal, still reads `fail` when no prompt arrives or it arrives
   unprefixed. A test that skips prints its reason. The plan names operator entries by their run text.
9. Before a live round the host is read (`hostwatch.py read --last 15`): a CONTENDED reading with a NEIGHBOUR
   named stops and is re-read, never retried into. The token window is the rig's own check, never a hand read; a
   start refused for it is uncounted — stop and say so.
10. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned
    user home. Read `df` before a whole rebuild.
11. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop
    and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop where you are.
12. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start; remove no scratch
    clone by a recursive delete — name it on the card instead. An entry that asserts a state a LATER step of the
    same plan ends is keyed to the round leg. Never write that the rig refuses a condition without the line that
    refuses it.
13. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the union or its standing
    list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` /
    `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

Its prompt holds a `## Cross-session` section only when the cross-session gate (below) is on: «Use `ListAgents` to discover targets … the name IS the address»; «A session that is not listed cannot be looked up … (An id or claude.ai/code link already in their message is the one exception: use the id as `to`.)»; «messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round»; «a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval … a session can refuse them outright»; «Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`». With the gate off the table reads «No one outside this session can be reached».

window: re-read your run dir `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-21T11-32-16Z-phase` and its `founder-forks.md` from disk
first and resume the take-up at P4 (the `research` row stands). Append the answers below to `founder-forks.md`,
snap this relay, take P4 on them and go on to the P5 card. No live start in this phase; no scheduled-wake or
timer tool. In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## The operator's own words — given in one dialog and read at 2026-11-21T12:10:30Z

1. **F1, the diagnostic reading: «Оба чтения, только имена (Recommended)».** Your option (a), IN THE NARROWED FORM
   he was shown and nothing wider: the sender's hooks write to disk ONLY the tool's name and, for the send, one
   boolean result — no arguments, no model text, no raw payload — and the stamp's `cross_session_probe` gains two
   closed-word keys: the tool names called (`send` · `search` · `list` · `other`) and the send's result class
   (`delivered` · `refused` · `none` · `unread`). He was told it also runs under the automatic verify in a
   user's real config, and that the raw-payload form was set aside because it would outlive a SIGKILL in the
   user's home. This is his ratification of that widening of the capture arm and of the stamp's content, over
   the rows your §4 names for F1, and nothing wider.
2. **The cap: «2 базовых + 1 запасной (Recommended)».** TWO base starts and ONE spare on one ledger, labels `XS`
   and `XS-2`, each in the shape shown to him: 2.1.328 by path, the rig's scratch home and private config, no
   key and no byte into any CLI dialog, one read of his credentials file by the rig, nothing written under his
   real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`, the sender's socket in the real `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cc-socks/` while it runs,
   the sender `claude -p` on Haiku. `XS` (`--cap 1`) diagnoses and, green at 29/29, records. `XS-2` (`--cap 2`)
   opens ONLY after a red that NAMES a cause and its mend through the revision door. The spare: the model's
   run-to-run variance, a rig refusal before the ledger line, or a host CONTENDED by a neighbour. A red stops
   implement. A third base start is his.
3. **The version: «2.1.328 (Recommended)».** The row is stamped on 2.1.328 alone; no 2.1.330 start; the one
   fixture set is re-recorded (32 → 33 files) on a 29/29 pass only.

## Technical answers (the overseer's)

5. **F2: path (A)** — diagnose, mend, re-record. (B) and (C) are declined for the reasons your block gives; (D)
   was offered to him and not chosen.
6. **The names-only capture mode is built as you proposed in your answer to my two questions:** a mode of the
   capture arm that never writes a payload — one small 0600 file of closed words, as the env-names file is. Its
   proof is the canary test over `tool_input`, `tool_response` and a model-text field PLUS a case that the mode
   leaves no payload file in the probe dir at all (so a SIGKILL leaves closed words only). Say in the plan what
   file a SIGKILL leaves and that its content is closed words; the residual row's words carry it.
7. **Read 2's field is unmeasured until `XS`:** the classifier reads a structured boolean only, in the shapes
   the tool's code states; any other or absent shape reads `unread`, never `refused`; a failed input validation

8. **`XS` must be able to name the cause in ONE start:** the plan writes, before the round, the table from

body:
1. **`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — the sender's closed words.** Beside `capture_plugin_files`
   (ledger.rs:557), pure functions over a payload's bytes that keep no byte of it:
   - `tool_word(payload) -> ToolWord` reads `tool_name` alone, as a string: `SendMessage` → `send`, `ToolSearch` →
     `search`, `ListAgents` → `list`, any other or an unparseable payload → `other`. The three names are compiled
     literals beside `SETTINGS_FLAG` (`SEND_TOOL`, `SEARCH_TOOL`, `LIST_TOOL`), read statically in the 2.1.328 bundle
     (research §Patterns detected), each a `viola verify` reading, never an assumption.
   - `send_result_word(payload) -> ResultWord` reads only a JSON boolean `success` at `tool_response.success` or
     `tool_response.data.success`, the two shapes the tool's own code states (`founder-forks.md` answers, item 7):
     `true` → `delivered`, `false` → `refused`; any other or absent shape → `unread`, never `refused`. No text match,
     no compiled message literal.
   - `tool_capture_document(event, tool, result)` returns `{"v":1,"event":"pre"|"post","tool":<word>,"result":<word|null>}`,
     and `tool_file_name(k)` = `Tool.<k>.json`; `parse_capture_file_name` does not parse it (`Tool` is no
     `HookEvent`), so `read_captures`, `free_k` and `ordinal` skip it as they skip `Env.<k>.json`.
   - `ProbePlugin::Sender`: its `hooks.json` holds exactly two groups, `PreToolUse` with no matcher and `PostToolUse`
     with matcher `SendMessage`, each `hook <event> --capture <dir> --names-only`; no spine event, no `--answers`.

2. **`src/cmd/hook.rs` — `--names-only`** (hidden, beside `--capture`, valid only with it). The arm reads stdin
   through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, classifies it in memory by step 1, and files ONLY `<dir>/Tool.<k>.json` — created by
   `create_private_new`, then `replace_private` at 0600 before any byte — and never the payload file
   (`file_from` is not reached). Every inertness rule holds: no `VIOLA_*` read, no obs init, no channel, nothing on
   stdout or stderr, exit 0, nothing written on a failure (`(security-plan · decision/hook-capture-arm)`,
   `(architecture · decision/probe-capture-arms-inert)`, `(obs-plan · decision/hidden-capture-arms-uninstrumented)`).
   Its doc comment names the operator's ratification (`inputs#I2` item 1). **What a SIGKILL of verify leaves** from
   it: only `Tool.<k>.json` files of closed words (and the plugin's two files naming viola's own pinned path and
   capture dir) under `<verify home>/ledger/probes/<pid>/`, never a payload.

3. **Unit cases** (`ledger.rs` tests, rstest tables, tests S1, a11y S4): `tool_word_names_the_four_classes` (each
   literal, an unknown name, an unparseable payload → `other`); `send_result_word_reads_only_the_boolean` —
   `case_1_success_true`, `case_2_success_false`, `case_3_data_success_true`, `case_4_data_success_false`,
   `case_5_success_a_string` (`unread`), `case_6_no_tool_response` (`unread`), `case_7_text_only_response`
   (`unread`); `sender_plugin_hooks_capture_names_only` (the two groups, the flag on each, no matcher on PreToolUse).
   Every oracle is a literal.

4. **The canary and no-payload cases** (`src/cmd/hook.rs` tests, and `tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs`, its
   binary already on the 20 s override; tests S2, S4; security S2):
   - `names_only_capture_files_closed_words_and_no_payload` (unit): a PreToolUse and a PostToolUse through
     `--names-only` leave exactly `Tool.1.json` and `Tool.2.json` in the dir, each mode 0600, each a literal JSON
     text; no `PreToolUse.*.json` or `PostToolUse.*.json` stands (`inputs#I2` item 6).
   - `names_only_capture_keeps_no_canary_byte` (subprocess, `viola hook pre-tool-use --capture <dir> --names-only`
     and `post-tool-use`): the payloads carry a canary in `tool_input.message`, in `tool_response` (`message` and a
     nested text) and in a model-text field; exit 0, stdout and stderr empty, and no canary byte stands in any file
     under the dir.
   - `names_only_capture_reads_unread_on_an_unknown_shape`: a PostToolUse whose `tool_response` is a string files
     `result: unread`.
5. **Phase A gates:** the first seven entries of §Test Commands, all green before phase B.

title: B. The row, its probe, the sender (tests S1–S5; security S1–S4; arch S1–S6; obs S1–S3; design S1–S3; layouts S1–S2)

data.head: ### B. The row, its probe, the sender (tests S1–S5; security S1–S4; arch S1–S6; obs S1–S3; design S1–S3; layouts S1–S2)

body:
6. **`ledger.rs` — the 29th row.** `CrossSessionPrefix` appended last to `ALL` (`[Self; 29]`), id
   `cross-session-prefix`, words `a message another session sends in opens with a harness prefix`. It reads `pass`
   or `fail` only (no `absent` arm).

7. **`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — `harness_prefix(prompt) -> Option<&'static str>`**, the closed id of
   the literal the raw start matches (no trim): `agent-message`, `task-notification`, `cross-session-escaped`,
   `cross-session`, in `HARNESS_PREFIX_IDS` beside `HARNESS_PREFIXES` (hook.rs:135-140). `prompt_origin` (hook.rs:265)
   is rewritten over it, its result unchanged; the four literals do not change. Unit cases: one per literal, an escaped
   tag and a leading space give `None`.

9. **`TypedRun.cross_session: Option<CrossSessionRun>`**: `prompts_before`, `sender` (`Exited` · `Failed` ·
   `Deadline`), `latency_ms`, and from the sender's `Tool.*.json` files in `k` order (each read through
   `take(MAX_FRAME)`): `sender_tools` (the `pre` files' words, in first-seen order, deduped; `none` when no file) and
   `send_result` (the `post` file's word; `none` when no `post` file stands — a send whose input failed validation
   fires none). **`ledger::cross_session_reading(trusted, typed)`** gives the outcome word and the prefix id:
   `not-run` · `sender-failed` · `sender-deadline` · `no-prompt` (no UserPromptSubmit past `prompts_before`) ·
   `unprefixed` (its `harness_prefix` is `None`) · `harness`. The row passes on `harness` alone; `sender_tools` and
   `send_result` decide nothing.

10. **`merge_stamp`** adds `measured.cross_session_probe` = `{outcome, prefix, latency_ms, sender_tools,
    send_result}`: closed words and one number (`(architecture · contract/ledger-stamps/content)`). `record`'s
    `named_payloads` adds `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`, the arrived prompt's capture, as a framing variant,
    through `scrubbed_payloads`; no sender file is ever recorded (`(security-plan · decision/fixture-scrub-and-refusal)`).

11. **Run B's cross-session turn** (`src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`, `turns.rs`, `typed.rs`):
    - **Run B's args** (`trusted_args`, runs.rs:104): the run's args, then `SETTINGS_FLAG` + `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`,
      then the plugin dir — `dialog_run`'s form (runs.rs:122).
    - **Where:** between the `/compact` paste's answer and the `/clear` paste (lean T1, standing), only when the box
      guard reads the box up and `ledger::resume_target` gives an id (ledger.rs:1174).
    - **The sender:** `run_bounded` with subject `verify-sender`: `program_args` + `-p <sender_prompt(id)> --model haiku
      --no-session-persistence --allowedTools SendMessage --plugin-dir <sender plugin>`, no `--settings`; cwd the print
      probe's `ProbeDir` (`Inputs` gains `sender_cwd` and `sender: RunDirs`, typed.rs:59); the sender plugin and its
      0700 captures dir inside it, written by `write_plugin` with `ProbePlugin::Sender`; the same R8 strip; bound
      `SENDER_DEADLINE` (120 s, beside `PROBE_DEADLINE`, verify.rs:45); stopped by the stop.
    - **The wait:** on exit 0, one more UserPromptSubmit up to `CROSS_SESSION_WINDOW` (30 s), then its turn's end up to
      the probe deadline; a non-zero exit or the deadline skips the wait. No retry inside one verify.
    - **After it:** the box guard re-read; up → `/clear` pasted and Run B ends by Ctrl-C as today; not up → no
      `/clear`, Run B ends by `end_by_kill`, no key (lean T2; `(architecture · decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs)`).

12. **`src/cmd/verify.rs`:** `measure` passes the sender inputs; `check_rows` checks 29 rows; `SENDER_DEADLINE`.
    **`schemas/diag-line.v1.json`** adds `verify-sender` to the `subject` enum (obs S2), `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`
    its case.

13. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs`,
    `test_cases_modes.rs`; fake-agent only; arch S3):
    - **Sender:** a `-p` prompt opening `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` is a sender. It reads the id, finds the registry
      row beside its exe whose `sessionId` is the id and whose process's parent pid equals its own parent pid, runs its
      `--plugin-dir`'s PreToolUse then PostToolUse hooks with SYNTHETIC compiled payloads (`tool_name` `SendMessage`,
      a `tool_response` of `{"success":true}`; named synthetic, `(test-plan · decision/synthetic-fixture-text)`), writes
      an empty 0600 `<exe dir>/inbox/<that pid>` and exits 0. No row, or a set holding no
      `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`: exit 1, nothing written, no hook.
    - **Receiver:** under `--framing`, an interactive fake polls its own inbox file only when its argv carries
      `--settings` equal to `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`; on the file it removes it, fires `UserPromptSubmit` variant
      `cross-session-1` as recorded, then ends the turn.
    - **`--cross-session-turn-screen <phase>`**, parsed beside `--tag-turn-screen`, for step 14's kill case alone.
    - Cases: `sender_delivers_only_to_its_siblings_session`, `sender_runs_its_plugin_hooks_names_only`,
      `receiver_fires_the_cross_session_variant_once`, `receiver_reads_no_inbox_without_the_accept_settings`.

14. **The row's fake-agent cases** (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, over a test-built synthetic set at a test-owned version,
    `tests/support/verify.rs` gaining the `cross-session-1` framing shape named SYNTHETIC; committed nowhere):
    - `cross_session_prefix_reads_pass_over_the_fake_sender`: step line `[29/29] cross-session-prefix … pass`; the
      stamp's `cross_session_probe` reads `outcome` `harness`, `prefix` `cross-session`, `sender_tools` `["send"]`,
      `send_result` `delivered`; one `verify-sender` process pair; Run B's receipt argv carries `--settings` then the
      literal; the sender's argv carries `--plugin-dir` and no `--settings`; `/clear` is pasted after the turn. (That the
      names-only mode files no payload is proven at step 4, not here: the probe dir is gone when verify exits.)
    - **The keeps-its-red case** (`inputs#I1` item 8), ONE rstest
      `cross_session_prefix_keeps_its_red_under_the_accept_settings`, Run B's argv carrying the literal in both:
      `case_1_no_prompt_arrives` (the set holds no `cross-session-1`: the fake sender exits 1, outcome `sender-failed`)
      and `case_2_arrives_unprefixed` (the synthetic prompt opens with plain text, outcome `unprefixed`); each reads
      `fail`, exit 1. The sender-exits-0 `no-prompt` path is held at unit level (step 15): over the fake it would wait
      out the 30 s window past the 20 s kill (`(test-plan · decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill)`).
    - `cross_session_prefix_ends_run_b_by_kill_when_the_box_is_not_up`: no Ctrl-C byte after the turn, no `/clear`.

15. **Unit cases** (`test_cases_checks.rs`, `test_cases_stamps.rs`, `test_cases.rs`, `test_cases_runs.rs`):
    `cross_session_prefix_passes_on_a_prefixed_arrival`; `cross_session_prefix_fails_when` — `case_1_not_run`,
    `case_2_no_prefix`, `case_3_no_prompt`, `case_4_sender_failed`, `case_5_sender_deadline`;
    `merge_stamp_writes_the_cross_session_block` (closed words only); a 28-row stamp reads unverified, a 29-row one
    verified; `framing_variants` names `cross-session-1`.

16. **Every relied-count literal moves to 29** — research's sweep, 94 hits in 9 files
    (`/28\]|28 pass|; 28\]|len\(\), 28|Some\("28"\)|\("rows", "28"\)`). `src/run/version_gate.rs` and
    `src/run/auto_verify.rs` tests step to 29. Each `cli_verify` summary literal moves by whether its Run B reaches
    step 11, read against its case's path, never re-counted to green. `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`'s
    `assert_framed_exit` (line 216) keys its expected failing lines on the variants a set holds: exit 0 only on a set
    holding both `question-permission` and `cross-session` variants; otherwise exactly the lines of the rows the set
    lacks read `fail`, the summary's fail count that number.

17. **The rig** (test-only, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`): `XS` and `XS-2` map to `Arm::VR`
    (mod.rs:210); `StampShape` keeps `XS` → `CROSS_STAMP` (`cross-stamp.json`), `XS-2` → `CROSS_STAMP_2`
    (`cross-stamp-2.json`) (`inputs#I2` item 9); `stamp_lines` (mod.rs:2817) prints `cross-session-prefix: <word>`,
    `cross-session: <outcome>`, `sender-tools: <words, space-joined | none>`, `send-result: <word>`, each `unread` with
    no entry; `FLOOR_ROWS` (mod.rs:78) takes the row, its rule «every relied row but four» kept; the label, stamp-shape
    and `stamp_lines` tables take the new rows.

18. **Phase B gates:** entries 8–14 of §Test Commands, then the three controls (§Test Commands), all green and «holds»
    before the round.

title: C. The round: `XS`, and only on its red, `XS-2` (`inputs#I2` item 2)

data.head: ### C. The round: `XS`, and only on its red, `XS-2` (`inputs#I2` item 2)

body:
19. **Read the host first**, by hand: `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py
    read --last 15`; its verdict line goes to `evidence/live-round.md`. A CONTENDED reading naming a NEIGHBOUR stops and
    is re-read later, never retried into; this repository's own gate stall is no neighbour.

20. **The round** (`gate.py run --chunk 2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row --run-dir {implement run dir}
    --live-legs`, or `--entry {n}`) fires in block order right before `XS`: the install read by path; `mise ls claude`
    (report-only); the census; the plain build and its hash; the kept record and stamp ABSENT; the kept `HF`/`HG`
    stamps' sha recorded once; the live home's stamp sha recorded once; the stale-socket count recorded once; the
    runtime dir owner-only; then `XS` under `--cap 1 --spare 1`. Disk state outside the tree, each an entry or true by
    construction with its code line (`inputs#I2` item 9):
    - `target/live-rig/XS/record/` and `target/live-rig/cross-stamp.json`: ABSENT, an entry (the record is never
      written over a standing dir, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:816`; the stamp by `place_private_new`).
    - `target/live-rig/floor-stamp.json`, `floor-stamp-2.json` (`HF`/`HG`'s kept products): PRESENT, their sha recorded
      before and read unchanged after; left as found.
    - A standing rig scratch home: true BY CONSTRUCTION, each start makes `<scratch base>/<run>` from the rig's own pid
      and start time (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/procs.rs:64-68`).
    - A standing `.viola-verify-*` dir: true BY CONSTRUCTION, `TrustedDir::create` removes a standing one
      (`src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs:301-304`).
    - The runtime dir: an entry; the sender's and Run B's sockets live under its `cc-socks/` while they run.
    A start refused for the token window or the host before its ledger line is uncounted: implement stops and says so.

21. **Right after the round:** the census keyed `operator`; the kept stamp read at `29 ok`; the cross-session block
    copied (report-only) into `evidence/live-round.md`; `HF`/`HG`'s stamps unchanged; the live home's stamp unmoved;
    no new stale socket; the record's names against the committed set. A round resumed at `XS` fires the round entries
    again.

22. **A red `XS`.** Implement records the rig summary whole (closed words) and fires the after-reads by `--entry`; then
    reads the cause off §Implementation notes' table, writes it to `evidence/live-round.md`, and STOPS. `XS-2`
    (`--cap 2 --spare 1`) opens only after a red that NAMES a cause, through the revision door with its mend. An
    ambiguous red is said as one; what start would split it is the operator's. The spare `XS-2` label is never spent
    on a red reading save that path: it covers the model's run-to-run variance, a rig refusal before the ledger line, or
    a host CONTENDED by a neighbour. A third base start is his.

23. **No key and no byte into any CLI dialog.** The rig types none; verify types only its compiled pastes; every probe
    dialog is answered by the capture hook's closed ids; the sender raises none; a held-message approval in Run B is
    never answered (step 11). From the real home the rig reads `~/.claude/.credentials.json` once (a 0600 copy removed
    on every exit) and stamps `~/.claude.json` read-only; nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`
    (`(security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty)`).

24. **Copy `target/live-rig/XS/record/2.1.328/` over `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/`**, a plain copy; the one new file joins
    (32 → 33, predicted: record what the copy measures) and `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` stays as committed.
    `evidence/landing.md` lists the files with sha256 prefixes before anything runs over the set; a file the hygiene
    suite refuses is a red, never scrubbed. `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` walks the `cross-session` framing stem.

25. **The reads over the landed set:** the `diff -r` entry; the unit, integration and E2E layers; the boot smoke. A
    drift, hygiene or ledger-probe red stops implement before the operator pass.

26. **`evidence/live-round.md`** records the host read, the rig summary whole, the ledger lines, the after-reads, the
    cause reading and every carry's disposition.
27. Pre-push, the hygiene read, then `rec.py land` and the pre-CI commit, then the push, then the CI read.
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json` — `XS`'s recorded cross-session arrival, through the scrub

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — the 29th row, `tool_word`, `send_result_word`, `tool_capture_document`, `tool_file_name`, `ProbePlugin::Sender`, the sender texts, `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`, `cross_session_reading`, the measured block, `TypedRun.cross_session`, `framing_variants`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases.rs` — row-count and verdict vectors at 29
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_checks.rs` — the row's pass and fail tables, the classifier tables
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` — the cross-session block, 28-row unverified, counts
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_runs.rs` — the `cross-session-1` framing variant
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `ALLOWED_TOOLS_FLAG` beside the flag literals
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — `harness_prefix`, `HARNESS_PREFIX_IDS`, `prompt_origin` over it, cases
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — `--names-only`, its doc comment, the names-only cases
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — `SENDER_DEADLINE`, the sender inputs, 29 step lines, the record's file
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — `Inputs` gains the sender's cwd and dirs
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs` — `trusted_args` with the literal; Run B's end by kill when the box is not up
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs` — the cross-session turn, the sender spawn, its waits, its `Tool.*` read
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — test module only, at 29
- `src/run/auto_verify.rs` — test module only, at 29
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — `verify-sender` in the subject enum
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the fake sender with its plugin hooks, the inbox receiver, the screen option
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs` — the registry lookup by session id and parent pid
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_modes.rs` — the four fake cases
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — the synthetic `cross-session-1` framing shape, named synthetic
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the row's fake cases, the keeps-its-red case, counts, process-line lists
- `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs` — relied and summary literals
- `tests/cli_verify/stamps.rs` — relied and summary literals
- `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` — `ROW_IDS` 29, the summary literal
- `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` — the framed-exit assertion keyed on the variants a set holds
- `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` — the `cross-session` stem
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` — the `verify-sender` subject case
- `tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs` — the names-only canary case
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — relied literals
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `XS` / `XS-2`, `CROSS_STAMP`, `CROSS_STAMP_2`, four summary lines, `FLOOR_ROWS`, cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — relied literals
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/` — re-recorded whole by `XS`; `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` kept

The block runs in this order: phase A (formatter, linter, the agent crate's and the root bin's unit cases, the canary
binary, then the workspace unit, integration and E2E layers on 28 rows); phase B (formatter, linter, the agent crate,
the rig's library cases, the root bin, the row's `cli_verify` cases, the canary binary); the round; the after-reads;
after the landing (`diff -r`, the three layers); the operator pass. What is not run, and why: no mutation run
(`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it); between phase B and the landing no
stamped-home suite runs (§Steps intro). Every test start runs under a test-owned home and user home; every waiting test
takes a bound under the 20 s lint. The live start runs under the rig's private scratch; the rig's `--deadline` bounds
it under the entry's `timeout`. The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it. `XS` is ledgered
in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row/evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`; `--cap` is the
running total of base lines in that one file. The census after the last live leg is keyed `operator`.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries; each reads «holds»
only when its own case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line:
| | `prefix-match` | `names-only-no-payload` | `unknown-shape-unread` |
| **File** | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` | `src/cmd/hook.rs` | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` |

| **The edit removes** | the clause of `cross_session_reading` that reads `unprefixed` when `harness_prefix` is `None` | the `--names-only` branch's return before `file_from` | the fall-through of `send_result_word` to `unread` (replaced by `refused`) |
| **Case** | `cross_session_prefix_fails_when::case_2_no_prefix` | `names_only_capture_files_closed_words_and_no_payload` | `send_result_word_reads_only_the_boolean::case_5_success_a_string` |

| **Fired on** | `cargo nextest run -p viola-agent-claude --no-fail-fast`, `--timeout 600` | `cargo nextest run -p viola --bin viola --no-fail-fast`, `--timeout 600` | the agent crate entry, `--timeout 600` |

title: I3-relay-xsession-p5.md.txt
body:
# The review of card 1 — «Cross-session prefix ledger row»

This relay, `relay-xsession-p3.md` and the phase directive are the only files of this folder you read or snap.
The plan stands in its design; **review — it returns to P4 for these, and only these** (all technical, the
overseer's; nothing of the operator's answers moves):

1. **The control ids.** `gate.py control` takes an id of 1–16 characters (`CONTROL_ID`, gate.py): `prefix-match`
   fits; `names-only-no-payload` (21) and `unknown-shape-unread` (20) would be refused at implement. Rename both
   within 16 and carry the names through the plan, the acceptance criteria and the card.
2. **The controls' entries are filtered to the guard's own cases** (the directive's item 8). As written each
   fires on a whole-package run (`-p viola-agent-claude`, `-p viola --bin viola`). Give each control a filtered
   command of its own — an `-E 'test(/…/)'` that selects its case (and, for the root-bin one, builds what the
   case needs) — with its `--timeout` named; say for each filter that it selects at least one test once the
   case exists.
3. **The three after-reads that assert a state OTHER actors move** — `kept-floor: unchanged`,
   `live-stamp: unmoved`, `stale-sockets: none added` — are keyed to the ROUND leg, right after `XS` (as the two
   name-diff entries are), so the wrap's light gate in a later window does not re-fire them: the live home's
   stamp moves by an ordered act of the overseer's whenever PATH's `claude` moves, and it is no red of this
   chunk hours later. Say that the whole-round command still fires with them in the span.
4. **`stale-sockets` is a READING, not a failing atom.** Seven and more other `claude` sessions live on this
   host; any of them ending between the two counts adds a dead socket this chunk did not make (the count
   stands at 141 already). Keep both counts printed and recorded in `evidence/live-round.md`; the entry's expect
   is its own echo line only. If the rig can name the pids it started (its census rows or its ledger), read the
   sockets of THOSE pids as the failing atom instead — say which the code allows, with the line.
5. On card 2: the changed entries named, every check re-run (the dry-run, planlint, the baselines and the
   must-pass / must-fail controls of the re-keyed entries), the plan's line count. Then stop for the word.
   Start nothing.

row.why: the overseer review of card 1: five technical points (control ids, filtered control entries, round-keyed after-reads, stale-sockets a reading, card 2 contents)

body:
18. **Phase B gates:** entries 8–14 of §Test Commands, then the three controls on their filtered entries (§Test Commands), all green and «holds»
    before the round.

21. **Right after the round:** the census keyed `operator`; the kept stamp read at `29 ok`; the cross-session block
    copied (report-only) into `evidence/live-round.md`; and, keyed to the round leg right after `XS`, `HF`/`HG`'s stamps
    unchanged, the live home's stamp unmoved, and the stale-socket counts printed (a reading); the record's names against the committed set. A round resumed at `XS` fires the round entries
    again.

The block runs in this order: phase A (formatter, linter, the agent crate's and the root bin's unit cases, the canary
binary, then the workspace unit, integration and E2E layers on 28 rows); phase B (formatter, linter, the agent crate,
the rig's library cases, the root bin, the row's `cli_verify` cases, the canary binary); the round (its after-reads of other actors' state keyed to the round leg right after `XS`: `gate.py run --live-legs`
fires them in its span, block order, and the wrap's light gate never re-fires them, `inputs#I3` item 3); the after-reads
of `XS`'s own products;
after the landing (`diff -r`, the three layers); the operator pass. What is not run, and why: no mutation run
(`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it); between phase B and the landing no
stamped-home suite runs (§Steps intro). Every test start runs under a test-owned home and user home; every waiting test
takes a bound under the 20 s lint. The live start runs under the rig's private scratch; the rig's `--deadline` bounds
it under the entry's `timeout`. The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it. `XS` is ledgered
in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row/evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`; `--cap` is the
running total of base lines in that one file. The census after the last live leg is keyed `operator`.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries; each fires on an
entry filtered to its guard's own cases (ids within 16 characters, `inputs#I3` items 1–2), and reads «holds» only when
its own case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line; each filter selects 0 tests on the untouched tree and at least one
once its case exists:
| | `prefix-match` | `no-payload` | `unread-shape` |

| **Fired on** | `cargo nextest run -p viola-agent-claude --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/cross_session_prefix_fails_when/)'`, `--timeout 300` | `cargo nextest run -p viola --bin viola --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/names_only_capture_files_closed_words_and_no_payload/)'`, `--timeout 600` | `cargo nextest run -p viola-agent-claude --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/send_result_word_reads_only_the_boolean/)'`, `--timeout 300` |

# Implement directive — «Cross-session prefix ledger row» (chunk 2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row)

The plan is approved (P5 card 2, plan rev 5). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents from the store and
its evidence dir from disk first. This directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. This session is driven
through the pinned product, which holds none of the last five mends: call no scheduled-wake or timer tool.

## The live cap for THIS chunk (the operator's own answers, read 2026-11-21T12:10:30Z; nothing widens it)

- **TWO base starts and ONE spare on one ledger (`evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`), claude 2.1.328 by path, under
  the rig's PRIVATE config and scratch home. THIS run makes ONE: `XS` (`--cap 1 --spare 1`)** — one
  `viola verify --record` of the 29-row tree, with the print-mode sender (`claude -p` on Haiku, its one allowed
  tool the CLI's own send, its capture plugin in the names-only mode) beside Run B; only verify's compiled pastes
  are typed; NO key and NO byte into any CLI dialog; a held-message approval in Run B is never answered; the
  kept stamp and the record stay under `target/live-rig/`.
- **`XS-2` is NOT this run's:** it opens only after a red that NAMES a cause, and its mend, through the phase's
  revision door. **A RED `XS` of any cause stops implement before the landing; no start follows it.** The spare is
  spent only on a start the rig refuses before its ledger line or a host CONTENDED by a neighbour — never on a
  red reading; the model's run-to-run variance is a spend the overseer names, not this run.
- **Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once by
  the rig (a 0600 copy, removed on every exit path). `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` is read for its sha alone,
  right before `XS`, and must read unmoved right after it. The pinned product is not rebuilt, replaced or
  re-pinned. This session runs claude 2.1.330; the start goes against 2.1.328 by path.
- **The sender's capture writes closed words only:** no payload, no argument, no model text reaches any file,
  stamp, fixture, log or message of yours. `sender-tools` and `send-result` are READINGS, never atoms.
- The start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made.

## The host

- Run nothing heavier than this chunk's own gate entries. Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole.
- **Before `XS`: STOP and say in one line that the round is ready** (phases A and B green, every control «holds»).
  The overseer arranges a quiet host window and sends the word to go on, with the time to read hostwatch FROM
  (`hostwatch.py read --from <UTC> --to <now>`). A CONTENDED reading that names a NEIGHBOUR makes no start: stop
  and say so.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.

## Stops

- **The plan's order is the order.** Phase A green on 28 rows; then phase B's cases and the three controls
  (`prefix-match`, `no-payload`, `unread-shape`), each fired on its own filtered entry, before the round. A
  control's record names the guard's OWN case as failed and lists by name any other case failing in it.
- **A RED `XS` stops implement BEFORE the landing and the operator pass.** Fire the after-reads by `--entry`,
  then report the start's own closed words: the row's word and `outcome`, `sender-tools`, `send-result`,
  `latency_ms`, and the cause as the plan's table reads that triple — said as AMBIGUOUS where the table says so.
  Nothing is retried on a red reading.
- An after-read that does not hold (the kept stamp short of 29, `kept-floor` or `live-stamp` moved, a name diff
  other than the two expected lines) stops before the landing. `stale-sockets` is a reading: both counts
  recorded.
- A red that would move a plan entry stops implement before the operator pass: say which entry and why.
- The carried rehearsal red (`rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del`) is acted on only at its next
  red: the printed rig summary and the kept frame read and the cause named BEFORE any mend; no retry, no
  loosened entry. A CI red on it is recorded and NOT re-run before the overseer's word.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone by a recursive delete: name it in the report.
- The rig keeps its frames, the record and the kept stamp locally until the landing copies the record; a file
  the hygiene suite refuses is a red, never scrubbed by hand; nothing of the operator's status line or config
  enters a commit. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home; no test starts a real `claude`. No leaf
  gains a figure the code states. No master row is reworded in this skill.

## On green

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.
End every process you start.

# Red analysis — XS (chunk 2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row)

Written 2026-11-21T13:55:22Z by the implement run `2026-11-21T13-20-00Z-implement`, answering `inputs#I6` (the
overseer's questions, snapped). Sources: the tree, this run's evidence (`live-round.md`, `cross-starts.ndjson`,
`28.log`), and the installed `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.328/claude` read as strings by byte offset
(`dd`-style windows, no start). **No start was made; no plan, master or code changed.** Bundle identifiers below are the
minifier's names in 2.1.328 (they collide across chunks, so each is cited with its byte offset); messages are named
by class, never quoted.

## Headline

**C4 holds by construction, and C2 cannot be the whole story.** In 2.1.328 the send tool never resolves a LOCAL
session by its bare session id. The resolver indexes local sessions by NAME only: the session's display name, or a
name derived from its cwd. A `name [ref]` form picks one of them by its ref. A bare UUID matches neither. It reaches
the resolver's `not-found` result, and the tool returns `success: false` (route `unresolved`, its telemetry error
class `not_reachable`, or `local_unlisted` / `timeout` when a list could not be read). That would be the reading with
the gate on, and it is exactly what `XS` read: `search send` · `refused` · `no-prompt`. The session id verify hands
the sender is the wrong ADDRESS FORM for this CLI. Whether the gate was also off is a second question no start has
answered. The id was refused before the gate could matter.

## A. `send`, `refused`

### A1. The `success: false` paths a plain-text send with `to` = a bare session id can reach

The tool's `deliver` (offset ≈348.33 M) for a string message, in order. "Reachable" is from the sender's argv and state:
`-p`, `--no-session-persistence`, the rig's fresh private config, the R8 strip, the print probe's cwd, `to` a bare
UUID, the message plain ASCII.

| # | Condition, in the bundle's terms | Reachable here? | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `QUo({to,message})` returns its refusal (only when `Fne()`, the subagent-sends scope, holds): the message is not a string, `to` has a uds/bridge/did scheme, a desktop id shape, an `@`, or fails `sq` | `Fne()` unread; a main-session `-p` sender is not a subagent, so likely not | a path the block did not name (subagent scope) |
| 2 | `Lt(writtenTo, to, session)`: a `name [id]` the listing tool printed, written differently from its listing | no — a bare id is its own normal form (`U$t` leaves it unchanged) | not C2/C4 |
| 3 | the sender is a subagent not allowed to send (`K7e`), or an observer (`N0o`) | no (main session) | not named |
| 4 | `Gs(to)`, a Claude Desktop `local_…` id with its tool unavailable, or a desktop refusal | no — a bare UUID is not the `local_` shape (`TD`, `CD` regex) | not named |
| 5 | scheme `bridge`/`uds` with the gate off (`!xl()`) → the gate-off class | no — a bare UUID is scheme `other` (`VS`) | C2 (unreachable for this `to`) |
| 6 | the resolver `sVn` → `me`: `Muo(to)` → `not-found` at once (a scheme ≠ other, a cloud/bridge id shape `fIi`, a socket path `uIi`, a desktop id `TD`, a text holding an id `hD`) | `hD` needs an opening bracket, `fIi` the `session_`/`cse_` prefix: a bare UUID trips none, so it goes on to the name lookup | — |
| 7 | the name lookup: team mailbox names, subagent names, then `Tee`'s `byName` (local sessions by `Ss(name)`), then a ≥3-char prefix match (`$e`) | **yes** — no local row is NAMED the UUID, so no exact or prefix key matches → `{kind:"not-found"}` | **C4** |
| 8 | `aSa(r)`: an own-agents-only refusal when `Fne()` holds and `r` is not an own agent | only if `Fne()` holds (unread) | not named (subagent scope) |
| 9 | `(r.kind local/cloud-session) && !xl()` → the gate-off class | no — `r` is `not-found` before this test | C2, past the point this send reached |
| 10 | `r` is this process's own socket or a self-claimed name (`Apn`, `vKn`, `nlt`) | no (the sender has no named session of its own) | not named |
| 11 | `r.kind === "not-found"` → the no-agent-named refusal, error class `not_reachable` (`local_unlisted` if the local list failed, `timeout` if a remote list timed out) | **yes — this is the path** | **C4** |
| 12 | `r.kind === "ambiguous"`, one exact match not settled (`ge`: a derived name, a bridge walk not settled or unavailable, a pin claimed) → a confirm-required refusal | not for a bare id (no match at all); **yes for a NAME** (see C) | not named — a name-path hazard |
| 13 | the uds delivery itself throws (the target gone or busy, `RKe`) | no — never reached | not named (target busy/gone) |
| 14 | the permission phase: a hook refusal, a denial, a handler rewrite (`degradedClass` `hook_refused` · `permission_denied` · `handler_rewrite`) | the sender's only plugin hooks are viola's names-only captures, which print nothing; a `-p` permission denial is possible in principle, but the tool's `checkPermissions` returns `allow` for a resolved local send outside the `isolatePeerMachines` case | a permission denial folded into the result: not excluded, but the sender's words show the call went past PreToolUse to a PostToolUse, which a hook or permission refusal before the call would not |

The paths the overseer named but the bundle does not show for this send:
- **The target busy or not idle:** only after a resolved uds send (#13). The send never resolved.
- **The target's inbound policy read at the SENDER:** none. The policy (`crossSessionInbound`) is read at the
  receiver (offset ≈341.93 M).
- **A sender with no inbox or socket of its own in `-p`:** supported, as a one-way send (`rVn` with `oneWay`). It is
  no refusal.
- **A sender absent from the roster because it does not persist:** the roster is read for the TARGET, never the
  sender.

**A refusal path that CANNOT be this one:** #5 (it needs a uds/bridge `to`), #4 (the desktop shape), #2. #9, the
gate-off refusal for a resolved local session, cannot be the path either, because it is tested only after the
resolver returned a local session, and a bare id never makes it return one.

### A2. C2 — the gate

`xl("send")` (offset 316 012 ≈ 760): it is off when the settings hold `messagingBeyondOwnAgentsDisabled`. Otherwise
it reads env `CLAUDE_CODE_HARBOR_KITE` when that is set. Otherwise (Linux) it reads the flag `b("tengu_harbor_kite",
true)`, whose second argument is the fallback the reader returns when no value is cached. A sibling gate in the same
chunk (`Ave`) tests `mn(…).source === "fallback"` explicitly, which shows the reader serves the fallback when nothing
is cached. So with a fresh private config holding no cached flag the gate reads **on**. Whether a `-p` start fetches
flags before its first tool call, and whether a fetch could bring `false`, is not settled by strings: **unread**. The
R8 strip removes `CLAUDE_CODE_HARBOR_KITE` from every verify child, so the env arm is never taken; the flag decides.
Whatever the gate read, the bare id is refused at #11 before the gate is tested for this `to` (A1 #9).

### A3. C4 — what a bare id is matched against

**Nothing.** `Tee` (offset ≈310.027 M) builds `byName` from each local roster row's `name`, or `g3(cwd)` (a cwd-derived
name) when the row has none, keyed by `Ss(name)` (lower-cased, dash-joined). A row's `sessionId` enters a candidate
only as `stableId`, behind the gate `tengu_session_stable_address` (default `false`), and its `claimedSessionIds` only
in the pin checks (`ne`, `vKn`). Neither is a lookup key. The tool's own prompt names the one id exception: a cloud or
Remote Control session id or a `claude.ai/code` link (`session_01…`, `cse_…`, the `bridge:` form, `Gl`/`Sz`). A local
UUID is not one of them. So the stale-id question does not arise:
- verify takes the id from Run B's first SessionStart `session_id` (`ledger::resume_target`);
- `/compact` keeps it (the row `local-command-compact` read pass in `XS`);
- the roster may well hold that id, but the send tool never looks it up by id.

### A4. `stale-sockets: before 141 after 146`

From the code alone, a reading:
- verify ends Runs A, C, D, E and F with `end_by_kill`, and Run B with Ctrl-C (`RunBEnd::CtrlC`: the box was up after
  the turn).
- A process ended by SIGKILL cannot unlink its own `cc-socks/<pid>.sock`. A Ctrl-C exit runs its cleanup.
- The `-p` print probe and the `-p` sender exit normally.
- So **up to five** of the five (A, C, D, E, F) can be the round's own, if each interactive child had bound its socket
  by the kill and the kill gave it no cleanup turn. The harness rule records portable-pty's kill as SIGHUP first,
  which may give one.
- Other sessions on the host also end in the window. The five are therefore not attributed: **unmeasured**.

## B. Readings that split what stays — closed words

After A, the one cause read from the code (C4, the address form) needs no start to name. What stays unread is a
gate that could ALSO be off, and the name path's own hazards (A1 #12). Each reading below, for a next start:

| Cause standing | Closed-word reading | Read from | Widens | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C2, the gate | `gate: on · off · unread`, the cached `tengu_harbor_kite` boolean in the rig's private config | the rig's private config file, after the start | the rig reads one VALUE (a boolean) of its own private config, where today it reads key names only: a widening the operator has not seen | the rig only |
| C4 under a name address | `roster: <n>`, the count of rows in `<private config>/sessions/` whose `name` equals the compiled Run B name | the rig's private config, read while Run B lives (the rig can count; verify must not) | the rig reads a roster row's `name` field by equality only, never kept: a widening the operator has not seen | the rig only |
| which address form the model wrote | `to-shape: bare-id · name-ref · name · uds · other`, the shape of `tool_input.to` | the sender's names-only PreToolUse capture | a third closed word in the names-only mode: a widening of the operator's F1 answer | a product change (`ledger.rs` + `hook.rs`) |
| why a send was refused | none in closed words: `tool_response` holds only `success` and the text; the route and error class (`not_reachable` …) go to the CLI's telemetry, not the hook payload | — | — | not obtainable without a text match (rejected, `inputs#I2` item 7) |
| a listing call | `list` already among `sender-tools` | the existing capture | nothing | nothing |

## C. The ways forward — priced, none decided

**(i) A diagnostic `XS-2`, then the mend, then a re-recording start.**
- A diagnostic run on the UNMENDED sender would only re-read C4, which the bundle already settles. Its one new fact
  would be the gate word, and only with the rig's widening.
- The least sequence is `XS-2` (diagnostic, base line 2 of 2), the mend through the revision door, then a recording
  start: **three base starts in all, one past the cap**. Two are spent or allotted; the third base start is the
  operator's. The spare covers only a rig refusal before its ledger line, or a contended host.

**(ii) A mend with no diagnostic start: address Run B by NAME.**
- **The mend:**
  - Start Run B with a compiled name (`-n`, which 2.1.328 offers as `--name`): a new flag literal and a ledger reading.
  - Widen the sender's tools to `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`.
  - Have the sender's prompt call `ListAgents`, then send to the entry of that compiled name with `to` exactly as
    printed, name and brackets. This is the form the tool's own refusal text asks for, and the ref path (`be(x, L,
    ref)`) resolves it without the one-match confirm (A1 #12).
- **Price:** one base start, the one left under the cap. The plan's revision covers:
  - the flag literal and `trusted_args`;
  - `sender_prompt` and `ALLOWED_TOOLS`;
  - the fake sender, which must resolve by name, not by session id;
  - the unit and `cli_verify` cases that pin the prompt;
  - the masters' rows on verify's child set and on the sender, where a new widening question for the operator stands:
    a named Run B leaves its name in the roster and in the resume picker.
- **What a red after it would still not tell:**
  - the gate (C2) against a permission denial of `ListAgents` in `-p` (`sender-tools` shows `list` only if it was
    called);
  - the model not following the two-step prompt;
  - the name path's confirm refusal if the model sent the bare name (A1 #12);
  - a receive-side hold, the C5-like case where the send reads `delivered` with no prompt.
  The existing words split some of these:
  - `list` absent → the model or a permission;
  - `send` + `refused` with `list` → the gate, or a confirm;
  - `delivered` + `no-prompt` → the receive side.
- **The other address, `uds:<path>`:** it is declined in this chunk's own constraints (`founder-forks.md` §3), so it
  is the operator's fork, not a mend this run may plan.

**(iii) The row leaves this chunk and this version.**
- **Stays useful from the uncommitted tree:**
  - `hook::harness_prefix` / `HARNESS_PREFIX_IDS` and `prompt_origin` over it (a refactor with its own cases);
  - the stamp's tolerance of unknown measured blocks;
  - the `cli_verify` helper changes that read `print` starts.
- **Cut** (it has no consumer without the sender; an unread capture mode is an unkillable mutant set, testing.md
  2026-09-24):
  - the names-only capture mode and its cases;
  - `ToolWord`/`ResultWord`;
  - the sender texts, `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS` and Run B's settings;
  - the cross-session turn in `turns.rs` and `runs.rs`;
  - the 29th row and every count back to 28;
  - the fake sender and receiver;
  - the rig's `XS` labels and four summary lines;
  - `verify-sender` in the schema.
- **Size:** a revision touching about 25 of the 29 changed files, most of it reverting. The `harness_prefix` part is
  a handful of lines in `hook.rs`.
- **What it leaves:** the HF/XS evidence, and this analysis's C4 reading, as the record of why path (A) with a bare
  id cannot pass on 2.1.328.

## What this run did not do

No start, no `XS-2`, no plan or master edit, no code edit since the round, and no text match. No value was read from
the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`; only the installed binary was read as strings.

flags before its first tool call, and whether a fetch could bring `false`, is not settled by strings: **unread**. The
R8 strip removes `CLAUDE_CODE_HARBOR_KITE` from every verify child, so the env arm is never taken; the flag decides.
Whatever the gate read, the bare id is refused at #11 before the gate is tested for this `to` (A1 #9).

### A3. C4 — what a bare id is matched against

**Nothing.** `Tee` (offset ≈310.027 M) builds `byName` from each local roster row's `name`, or `g3(cwd)` (a cwd-derived
name) when the row has none, keyed by `Ss(name)` (lower-cased, dash-joined). A row's `sessionId` enters a candidate
only as `stableId`, behind the gate `tengu_session_stable_address` (default `false`), and its `claimedSessionIds` only
in the pin checks (`ne`, `vKn`). Neither is a lookup key. The tool's own prompt names the one id exception: a cloud or
Remote Control session id or a `claude.ai/code` link (`session_01…`, `cse_…`, the `bridge:` form, `Gl`/`Sz`). A local
UUID is not one of them. So the stale-id question does not arise:
- verify takes the id from Run B's first SessionStart `session_id` (`ledger::resume_target`);
- `/compact` keeps it (the row `local-command-compact` read pass in `XS`);
- the roster may well hold that id, but the send tool never looks it up by id.

### A4. `stale-sockets: before 141 after 146`

From the code alone, a reading:
- verify ends Runs A, C, D, E and F with `end_by_kill`, and Run B with Ctrl-C (`RunBEnd::CtrlC`: the box was up after
  the turn).
- A process ended by SIGKILL cannot unlink its own `cc-socks/<pid>.sock`. A Ctrl-C exit runs its cleanup.
- The `-p` print probe and the `-p` sender exit normally.
- So **up to five** of the five (A, C, D, E, F) can be the round's own, if each interactive child had bound its socket
  by the kill and the kill gave it no cleanup turn. The harness rule records portable-pty's kill as SIGHUP first,
  which may give one.
- Other sessions on the host also end in the window. The five are therefore not attributed: **unmeasured**.

## B. Readings that split what stays — closed words

After A, the one cause read from the code (C4, the address form) needs no start to name. What stays unread is a
gate that could ALSO be off, and the name path's own hazards (A1 #12). Each reading below, for a next start:

| Cause standing | Closed-word reading | Read from | Widens | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C2, the gate | `gate: on · off · unread`, the cached `tengu_harbor_kite` boolean in the rig's private config | the rig's private config file, after the start | the rig reads one VALUE (a boolean) of its own private config, where today it reads key names only: a widening the operator has not seen | the rig only |
| C4 under a name address | `roster: <n>`, the count of rows in `<private config>/sessions/` whose `name` equals the compiled Run B name | the rig's private config, read while Run B lives (the rig can count; verify must not) | the rig reads a roster row's `name` field by equality only, never kept: a widening the operator has not seen | the rig only |
| which address form the model wrote | `to-shape: bare-id · name-ref · name · uds · other`, the shape of `tool_input.to` | the sender's names-only PreToolUse capture | a third closed word in the names-only mode: a widening of the operator's F1 answer | a product change (`ledger.rs` + `hook.rs`) |
| why a send was refused | none in closed words: `tool_response` holds only `success` and the text; the route and error class (`not_reachable` …) go to the CLI's telemetry, not the hook payload | — | — | not obtainable without a text match (rejected, `inputs#I2` item 7) |
| a listing call | `list` already among `sender-tools` | the existing capture | nothing | nothing |

## C. The ways forward — priced, none decided

**(i) A diagnostic `XS-2`, then the mend, then a re-recording start.**
- A diagnostic run on the UNMENDED sender would only re-read C4, which the bundle already settles. Its one new fact
  would be the gate word, and only with the rig's widening.
- The least sequence is `XS-2` (diagnostic, base line 2 of 2), the mend through the revision door, then a recording
  start: **three base starts in all, one past the cap**. Two are spent or allotted; the third base start is the
  operator's. The spare covers only a rig refusal before its ledger line, or a contended host.

**(ii) A mend with no diagnostic start: address Run B by NAME.**
- **The mend:**
  - Start Run B with a compiled name (`-n`, which 2.1.328 offers as `--name`): a new flag literal and a ledger reading.
  - Widen the sender's tools to `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`.
  - Have the sender's prompt call `ListAgents`, then send to the entry of that compiled name with `to` exactly as
    printed, name and brackets. This is the form the tool's own refusal text asks for, and the ref path (`be(x, L,
    ref)`) resolves it without the one-match confirm (A1 #12).
- **Price:** one base start, the one left under the cap. The plan's revision covers:
  - the flag literal and `trusted_args`;
  - `sender_prompt` and `ALLOWED_TOOLS`;
  - the fake sender, which must resolve by name, not by session id;
  - the unit and `cli_verify` cases that pin the prompt;
  - the masters' rows on verify's child set and on the sender, where a new widening question for the operator stands:
    a named Run B leaves its name in the roster and in the resume picker.
- **What a red after it would still not tell:**
  - the gate (C2) against a permission denial of `ListAgents` in `-p` (`sender-tools` shows `list` only if it was
    called);
  - the model not following the two-step prompt;
  - the name path's confirm refusal if the model sent the bare name (A1 #12);
  - a receive-side hold, the C5-like case where the send reads `delivered` with no prompt.
  The existing words split some of these:
  - `list` absent → the model or a permission;
  - `send` + `refused` with `list` → the gate, or a confirm;
  - `delivered` + `no-prompt` → the receive side.
- **The other address, `uds:<path>`:** it is declined in this chunk's own constraints (`founder-forks.md` §3), so it
  is the operator's fork, not a mend this run may plan.

**(iii) The row leaves this chunk and this version.**
- **Stays useful from the uncommitted tree:**
  - `hook::harness_prefix` / `HARNESS_PREFIX_IDS` and `prompt_origin` over it (a refactor with its own cases);
  - the stamp's tolerance of unknown measured blocks;
  - the `cli_verify` helper changes that read `print` starts.
- **Cut** (it has no consumer without the sender; an unread capture mode is an unkillable mutant set, testing.md
  2026-09-24):
  - the names-only capture mode and its cases;
  - `ToolWord`/`ResultWord`;
  - the sender texts, `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS` and Run B's settings;
  - the cross-session turn in `turns.rs` and `runs.rs`;
  - the 29th row and every count back to 28;
  - the fake sender and receiver;
  - the rig's `XS` labels and four summary lines;
  - `verify-sender` in the schema.
- **Size:** a revision touching about 25 of the 29 changed files, most of it reverting. The `harness_prefix` part is
  a handful of lines in `hook.rs`.
- **What it leaves:** the HF/XS evidence, and this analysis's C4 reading, as the record of why path (A) with a bare
  id cannot pass on 2.1.328.

## D. Two follow-ups (the overseer's, answered from the bundle, no start)

### D1. The uds form (`to` = `uds:<path>`)
- **Building the path:**
  - 2.1.328 accepts a socket file named `<digits>.sock`, `<digits>-<8 hex>.sock` or `<1–16 hex>.sock`, in
    `/run/user/<uid>/cc-socks` or `/tmp/cc-socks[-<uid>]` (`yz` and `qJ`, offset ≈308.894 M).
  - Verify holds Run B's child pid (`Run::child_pid`) and the runtime dir's NAME (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`), so it can
    compose `<runtime>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock` with no directory read, but only for the bare-pid form.
  - Which of the three forms Run B's CLI uses is not settled by strings. The research's host read saw `<pid>.sock`.
  - A `-<8 hex>` suffix would make the path unbuildable without a read. That is **unread**.
- **The sender's authentication:**
  - The send needs no roster row: `deliver`'s uds branch calls `sendToUdsSocket` (`rli`) straight on the path.
  - `Ae` (offset 316 196 887) reads the receiver's peer token from `<config dir>/sessions/<pid>.<sha256(socket
    path)>.key` (`snl`/`Fds`), where `<config dir>` is the SENDER's config dir.
  - Run B and the sender run under the same config (the rig's private one, or the user's own under a plain or
    automatic verify), so the key is found when Run B wired its inbox.
  - On Linux a missing key is NOT refused at the sender: `requireLiveOwner` applies on Windows only, and the frame
    goes out with no token. Whether Run B then drops an unvouched frame is a receive-side fact: **unread**.
  - The connect itself checks: a usable local path (`sq`), no symlink at the path (`noFollowSymlink`), and a 5 s
    timeout.
- **The arrival:**
  - The name path, once resolved to a local session, sends through the same `sendToUdsSocket` to that session's
    socket. So a uds send is the same wire frame, and Run B's inbound code builds its prompt the same way whichever
    `to` the sender wrote.
  - The prefix (escaped or plain tag) is Run B's choice either way. Its live form on 2.1.328 is **unmeasured**.
- **Refusal paths that remain:**
  - **The gate:** `validateInput` refuses a uds `to` when `xl()` is off. It fires before the tool runs, so the
    sender's words would read `send` with `send_result` `none`.
  - **Self:** the path is the sender's own socket (`nlt`). Not reachable here.
  - **The hop-loop pause** (`iVn`). Not reachable on a first send.
  - **A thrown send**, after which the tool reads `refused`:
    - a non-local path or a symlink;
    - the 5 s timeout;
    - the socket gone (`ENOENT` / refused, as when Run B ended);
    - the inbox rate limit (`paced`).
  - **On receipt, not a send refusal:** Run B's inbound policy (`accept` here), its startup hold, the kill switch.
  - **Standing:** the socket form is declined in this chunk's constraints (`founder-forks.md` §3). It is the operator's
    fork.

### D2. A bare compiled NAME from `--name`, with no `ListAgents` call
- **Resolution:** `me` → `gse(name)` is null (no brackets) → the local rows from the roster (`KUo`) → `Tee`'s
  `byName.get(Ss(name))`. One live row named so is ONE candidate, `kind: session`, `where: this-machine`. `Dnn`
  returns `ambiguous` for any non-in-process candidate, so `ge` decides.
- **No confirm (path #12 does NOT fire)** only when ALL of these hold:
  - exactly one candidate;
  - its name is not derived (a `--name` row has `nameSource: "user"`, so `derivedName` is false);
  - the remote lists settled: the Remote Control walk (`X`, run first because `Ce` holds for a lone session
    candidate) returned with no `timeout` / `fetch_failed`, the cloud list (`Zft`) is not unavailable, and the local
    list (`KUo`) is not unavailable;
  - no pinned identity is claimed locally for that name;
  - the name was not pinned to an agent.
  Then `ge` returns the local session `exactUnique` and the send goes to its socket.
- **Otherwise #12 fires:** the confirm-required refusal (`degradedClass` `confirm_required`, `success: false`).
- **What breaks uniqueness or settlement in a real config:**
  - a second live session of the same name in the same config's roster: two verifies at once share a compiled name
    (under the automatic verify, the user's own config);
  - a cloud or Remote Control session of the account titled the same, since remote rows join `byName` beside the
    local ones;
  - the Remote Control walk or the cloud fetch timing out or failing cold under a `-p` start's fresh credentials.
    This is the likeliest in the rig's private config, and it is **unmeasured**;
  - an earlier pin in the same conversation; none in a fresh `-p` sender.
- **What a name with pid or random parts buys:** making the compiled name unique per verify (a pid in it) answers
  the first cause. The rest stay network- and account-dependent. Only the `name [ref]` form the listing prints skips
  the one-match check (`be(x, L, ref)`), and that needs the `ListAgents` call this follow-up leaves out.

## What this run did not do

No start, no `XS-2`, no plan or master edit, no code edit since the round, and no text match. No value was read from
the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`; only the installed binary was read as strings.

# The operator's answer after the red `XS` — «Cross-session prefix ledger row»: a plan REVISION

Read at 2026-11-21T14:00:25Z, his dialog in the overseer's session, after `evidence/red-analysis.md` (its §A–§D). This relay,
the earlier relays of this chunk and the phase directive are the only files of this folder you read or snap. It
goes with a plan REVISION through the phase's door, in a NEW phase run, in a fresh window: read the chunk's
documents, its evidence dir and `red-analysis.md` from disk first. No live start in the revision; no
scheduled-wake or timer tool; no compiled screen literal printed in chat.

## The operator's own word

1. **The address: «По сокету Run B (Recommended)».** The cause stands as your analysis reads it from the bundle —
   the send tool never resolves a local session by a bare session id (C4, the address form). The mend he chose:
   **verify COMPOSES Run B's socket address itself** — `uds:<runtime dir>/cc-socks/<Run B's child pid>.sock`, from
   the pid of its own child and the runtime dir's name — **with NO directory read, no session listing and no
   name**, and hands it to the sender as `to`. He was shown, in the option's words: that the target is then
   exactly one and the misaddressing residual into another live session goes away; that verify relies on the
   socket file's name form (`<pid>.sock` as seen on this host), and a CLI that names it otherwise reads the
   start RED, never a false pass; and that this is the address set aside yesterday as «a read» — now without a
   read, and a widening new to him. This is his ratification of that widening and nothing wider. The name
   paths (with or without a listing) and dropping the row are declined.
2. **The cap is unchanged:** the mended start is `XS-2` (`--cap 2 --spare 1`, the ledger's second base line),
   in the same shape as `XS`; the spare unspent. A red `XS-2` stops implement; a third base start is his.

## Technical (the overseer's)

3. **The path is composed, never probed by verify:** no `stat`, no listing, no symlink test of its own — the
   CLI's connect does its own checks. If the composed path is wrong the sender's words say so (`send` with
   `refused` or `none`) and the row reads `fail`. The sender's prompt carries the `uds:` address as its one
   target; the bare session id leaves the prompt. The runtime dir comes from the env name verify already hands
   its children; say which line.
4. **Extend the cause table for the uds form** before the round, from your §D1: gate off → `send` · `none`
   (refused at input validation); a thrown send (path form wrong, socket gone, timeout, paced) → `send` ·
   `refused`; `delivered` with no prompt → the receive side (the peer key missing, the startup hold, the kill
   switch); each said as named or AMBIGUOUS.
5. **The peer key:** the sender finds Run B's key under the config dir both run in; say in the plan that verify
   reads nothing of it, and what the residual row's words carry for a frame sent with no token (unmeasured).
6. **What the mend removes:** W3's words change — the misaddressing residual is no longer «lowered by naming one
   id» but closed by address, save a pid reused between compose and send (say how verify bounds it: Run B is
   its own live child for the whole send). Every reached master row is named again in the revision's block of
   expected amendments; a row the uds form reaches that §4 of the P3 block did not name is a fork in
   `founder-forks.md`.
7. **`XS-2`'s on-disk needs:** `cross-stamp-2.json` and `target/live-rig/XS-2/record` ABSENT before; `XS`'s kept
   `cross-stamp.json` PRESENT and unchanged before and after, beside `HF`/`HG`'s; the live-home sha RE-TAKEN
   right before `XS-2` into a file keyed to it; the stale-socket reading re-taken likewise. Entries that read
   `XS`'s products (the `29 ok` read, the name diff, the `diff -r`) move to `XS-2`'s.
8. **The round must fire as ONE command this time:** the tool refused the whole round because an operator entry
   and leg-less entries stood inside its span, and three round after-reads were then run by hand. Re-order the
   block so the span holds round and live entries only (the census keyed `operator` and the leg-less reads
   after the span), and say on the card that the whole-round dry-run accepts it.
9. The controls, the names-only mode, the fake sender's cases and every count stand; the fake sender resolves
   its target by the uds address it is given. The plan's stale notes («controls fire on this entry» on the two
   whole-package entries; «the first seven entries») are corrected on the way.
10. On the card: the changed steps and entries named, every check re-run, and the four deviations of the stopped
    run folded as plan text. Then stop for the word. The seam after P5 stands.

body:
- **Implement re-enters at step 8.** It writes the address change through steps 8–15, then fires entries 9–19 and the
  four controls (step 18). Then comes the host read (step 19), then the round as ONE call. Entries 1–8 are not re-fired:
